name: Calendar Done
description: 📅✅ marks something as locked in, scheduled, and confirmed. It's what you send when a plan moves from 'maybe' to 'definitely happening' or when a deadline just got met.
meaning: The calendar shows the date or timing, and the checkmark seals it as done or approved. Together they say 'this is on the books and it's final' — a plan that's both scheduled and guaranteed.
examples: got the meeting booked for tuesday 📅✅
seoDescription: What does 📅✅ mean? It signals a date or deadline that's confirmed and locked in — a plan that's both scheduled and final.

longForm.overview:
📅✅ is the combo that turns a date into a commitment. The calendar emoji alone just marks a time; the checkmark turns that time into something guaranteed. Together they form the emoji equivalent of writing something down and circling it — this is happening, and it's confirmed.

What makes this combo work is that it solves a specific problem in group chats and work channels: you need to signal both 'when' and 'it's locked.' A single 📅 can feel tentative. A single ✅ without a date can feel abstract. Pairing them makes the message concrete and final. People send 📅✅ when they want to close a conversation about timing, when a plan has moved from discussion phase to scheduled phase.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
📅✅ shows up after someone suggests a date and it gets approved — a meeting time confirmed, a trip finalized, a deadline set. It also lands on its own when someone is announcing that something is officially scheduled. In work Slack channels it's the standard reply when a date gets locked in after back-and-forth. In group chats it's what people send after they've booked the restaurant or confirmed the flight.

You'll see it paired with specific dates ('next tuesday 📅✅') or used standalone after a scheduling conversation has ended. It signals relief — the planning is over, the date is real, everyone can stop negotiating.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 📅✅ if the plan is still up in the air or if you're just proposing a date. Sending it too early reads as presumptuous, like you're forcing agreement before discussion is done. Also avoid it in contexts where you're just mentioning a date casually — 'I'm thinking about going in may' doesn't need 📅✅, only 'I booked my flight for may 15th' does.

Don't use it to confirm someone else's plan without their input. A single ✅ or a sentence like 'sounds good' respects that they might still be adjusting. Reserve 📅✅ for dates you personally locked in or for plans where the group has genuinely reached consensus.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 📅✅, a simple acknowledgment works — 'got it' or 'perfect' or a mirror 📅✅ of your own. If you need to change the date, do it immediately before the checkmark settles into everyone's minds. A sentence like 'actually can we move it to the 14th' is clearer than trying to signal doubt with an emoji.

If 📅✅ lands on a plan you made, you can reply with your own 📅✅ to affirm it's locked. If it's on someone else's announcement in a group chat, you don't need to reply — the checkmark has done the work. The combo is final enough that silence reads as agreement.

faqs.question: Can I use 📅✅ if we're still deciding on the date
faqs.answer: No — that reads as you forcing agreement. Use 📅✅ only after the date is actually decided. While you're still discussing, stick with 📅 alone or just type out your suggestion.

faqs.question: Does 📅✅ mean the plan is definitely happening
faqs.answer: Yes, it means locked in and confirmed. The checkmark makes it final, not provisional. If there's any chance of cancellation or rescheduling, don't send it yet.

faqs.question: What's the difference between 📅✅ and just ✅
faqs.answer: ✅ alone means 'done' or 'approved,' but it doesn't specify when. 📅✅ adds the timing element — it's not just approved, it's scheduled and set for a specific date.

faqs.question: Is 📅✅ appropriate for work messages
faqs.answer: Yes, it's standard in work channels for confirming meeting times, project deadlines, and event dates. It's direct and professional without being stiff.

conversationExamples.message: sprint review is scheduled for thursday at 2pm 📅✅
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is confirming the meeting time is locked and everyone should add it to their calendar. This is a final announcement — no more discussion about timing. Reply with acknowledgment or add it to your calendar immediately.

conversationExamples.message: road trip booked for labor day weekend 📅✅
conversationExamples.interpretation: The trip is officially happening on those dates. The sender has confirmed transportation, lodging, or both. This is your signal to request time off work and start packing. Reply with excitement or a mirror 📅✅ to show you're in.

The date is scheduled and confirmed. The sender has put in effort to book a specific time and place, which signals genuine interest. This is not tentative — they're telling you when to show up. Reply with confirmation or let them know immediately if something changed.

conversationExamples.message: thanksgiving at our place this year 📅✅
conversationExamples.interpretation: The family gathering location and date are decided. This closes any debate about where the holiday will happen. Older relatives will interpret this as a firm plan. Reply with confirmation or flag conflicts right away before everyone commits.
The release date is official and finalized. This is the artist or label confirming no delays. Fans should mark their calendars. Reply with hype or a mirror emoji to show you're ready.
